## Purpose {.unnumbered .unlisted}

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{marginfigure}
\resizebox{0.92\linewidth}{!}{\mlphysicalstackfull{20}{100}{20}{20}{20}}
\end{marginfigure}
:::

_Why does an admitted plan still need permission on every control tick?_

A trajectory can be feasible when it arrives and become unsafe while the machine follows it. The body lags its reference, a payload or a hot motor erodes braking authority, a person steps into the path, or the learned proposer stalls with its last command still in force. A machine that checks only before motion begins discovers these changes after the energy is already moving, and the proposer cannot be trusted to notice them, because nothing in its output bounds stopping distance, actuator effort, or timing. Learned proposals therefore need an independent permission path that re-checks current conditions on every tick, keeps useful motion inside a stopping envelope, corrects a command when a feasible correction exists, and holds a response it can execute without the proposer before the remaining margin is spent. Each of those guarantees depends on bounded sensing error, available actuator force, and a decision delivered on time. Enforcement joins these conditions at the causal boundary, where a permitted command becomes motion that software cannot undo.

{{< pagebreak >}}

::: {.callout-learning-objectives}

- Explain the relationship between tracking accuracy, command permission, and independent enforcement at the actuator boundary
- Calculate the finished stopping budget and the speed ceiling it sets from response delay, braking, localization, and tracking error
- Derive how momentum and commanded effort change the remaining safety margin
- Explain how a control barrier function limits motion while its model, sensing, actuator, and timing assumptions hold
- Formulate a quadratic program that minimally adjusts a proposal within feasible actuator and safety constraints
- Select state-matched fallback responses when sensing, computation, or actuator limits invalidate normal enforcement
- Distinguish the permission path's unrated performance checks from the certified drive, scanner, and arm safety functions that carry the protective claim beneath it
- Construct an enforcement record and formulate the admitted command that binds each check to its detector, its fallback response, and the records it consumes

:::

## Deterministic Safety Filters and Permission Gating {#sec-enforcement-deterministic-gatekeeper}

Every physical AI system ends in the same act. A command leaves software, becomes current in a motor winding, and puts momentum into a world that does not roll back. Safety enforcement is the runtime mechanism that decides, one control tick at a time, whether the next command may cross that causal boundary. Checking a plan once before it runs does not settle the question, because admission judges the plan against the state the planner predicted, and the machine then executes it against the state it actually reaches. Between those two moments the body can lag its reference, an actuator can run short of torque, a person can step into the aisle, and the learned proposer can stall or emit a setpoint the plan never contained. Enforcement exists so that none of these events is discovered only after the energy has been delivered.

The central constraint is that the learned proposer can neither be trusted with that decision nor be discarded. Its competence is what makes the machine useful, yet nothing in its output bounds stopping distance, actuator effort, or timing. Enforcement resolves the tension by separating proposal from permission (principle \ref{pri-vol4-proposal-permission}) and giving the permission side three jobs. It must hold a stopping reservation, the clearance the machine needs to arrest its motion from the current state; it must correct a proposal minimally when a feasible correction exists; and it must select a response it can execute without the proposer when none does. We develop these in that order. The tracking bound and the stopping budget fix the reservation and the speed it allows. Actuator authority and the control barrier function turn the reservation into a constraint on the next command. The least-change filter and its cycle budget make the correction timely. The fallback ladder, and the certified safety functions beneath it, supply the response that survives a failed check, and the enforcement record binds every check to its evidence.

On the warehouse mobile manipulator, the safety microcontroller (MCU) admits the run down the aisle only after the matched stop suffix named in its trajectory record (@sec-planning-trajectory-contract) is resident in the MCU's memory and feasible from its commitment entry state. Admission also requires an independently executable, state-matched fallback from every state reachable during the admitted motion before commitment; the attached suffix need not fit those earlier states. That admission checks the plan once, before the motion starts. The machine then executes it one millisecond tick at a time, and enforcement is the check made on every one of those ticks, together with the response it selects when even the resident stop no longer fits.

An invalid command must be intercepted before it reaches the drive, because once current in a winding imparts momentum, an exception handler cannot recall it (@sec-boundary-bedrock-laws). Enforcement therefore keeps the task competence of learned policies while denying them authority over geometric clearance, thermal limits, and human-safety invariants. The enforcer\index{Enforcer} of @sec-nervous-cadences, the permission path's per-tick gatekeeper, sits on the permission side of the proposal boundary. It is a hard real-time component that evaluates candidate proposals, verifies invariant state bounds, and holds the exclusive hardware authority to permit current flow or command a fallback stop.

::: {.column-margin}
![](images/svg/spa_locator_pa.svg){width="100%" fig-alt="S·P·A locator triad highlighting the Plan-to-Act gating edge."}
*The Plan $\cap$ Act gatekeeper: enforcing forward invariance and arresting unsafe proposals at the physical boundary.*
:::

In the architecture this chapter follows, the enforcer executes on a dedicated microcontroller wired to the sensing and drive interfaces it needs. It checks each candidate command before the drive can apply it. A packet firewall offers a limited software analogy: a sender may request an operation without having authority to perform it. Unlike a packet filter, the enforcer must also account for momentum already present in the plant and preserve an achievable response when it refuses a request.

The architecture separates a capable proposer, a resident protective controller, and an output selector. This is the **Simplex architecture**\index{Simplex architecture!dual-controller model} [@sha2001using]: the proposer supplies useful candidates, while the permission path retains the exclusive ability to select a physically feasible response without waiting for it. The hardware allocation that makes this separation effective is developed in @sec-placement. The first quantity the enforcer needs is how far the body can stray from the reference it is asked to follow, because every clearance the permission path defends must also contain that error.

```{python}
#| label: calc-enforcement-lease-stop
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ TIMING CONTRACT AND THE LEASE-EXPIRY WORST CASE
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: the lease paragraph below; the cycle timeline, @tbl-12-fallback-hierarchy,
# │          the enforcement record, and the summary reuse these strings.
# │ Goal:    state the three timers and the delay from last renewal to brake onset.
# │ Show:    chunk rate, lease, heartbeat rate and timeout, self-watchdog,
# │          tick, bus cycle, brake onset, renewal-to-onset delay; the
# │          evidence-age refusal threshold (budgeted observation age plus the
# │          clock-conversion bound) read by cycle stage 2 and the record. The
# │          base stall is priced in calc-enforcement-stopping-budget, after the
# │          spare is set.
# │ How:     the same RM/AISLE fields that size the lease in @sec-nervous-cadences.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt, fmt_latency, fmt_frequency, check

RM = Embodied.MobileManipulator.WarehouseMobileManipulator
AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle

class EnforcementLeaseStop:
    # ┌── 1. LOAD ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    chunk_rate = RM.chunk_rate  # category: chosen
    lease = AISLE.t_lease  # category: chosen
    heartbeat_rate = AISLE.heartbeat_rate  # category: chosen
    heartbeat_timeout = AISLE.heartbeat_timeout  # category: chosen
    self_watchdog = AISLE.mcu_self_watchdog  # category: chosen
    tick = AISLE.t_tick  # category: chosen
    bus = AISLE.t_bus  # category: illustrative
    onset = AISLE.t_brake_onset  # category: illustrative
    t_age = AISLE.perception_age  # category: derived (observation age the budget charges, row 5)
    eps_sync = 0.2 * millisecond  # category: illustrative (clock-conversion bound, @sec-perception-observation-contract)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    chunk_period = (1 / chunk_rate).to(millisecond)
    renewal_to_onset = (lease + tick + bus + onset).to(millisecond)
    age_threshold = (t_age + eps_sync).to(millisecond)  # dispatch-age qualification threshold

    # ┌── 3. GUARD ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    check(chunk_period < lease, "One chunk period must fit inside the lease.")
    check(heartbeat_timeout < lease, "A total host stall must trip the heartbeat before the lease expires.")
    check(abs(lease.to(millisecond).magnitude - 60.0) < 1e-9, "The chunk lease is 60 ms.")
    check(abs(renewal_to_onset.magnitude - 82.0) < 1e-9, "Brake onset comes 82 ms after the last valid renewal.")
    check(abs(t_age.to(millisecond).magnitude - 51.6) < 0.05, "The budgeted observation age is 51.6 ms.")
    check(abs(age_threshold.magnitude - 51.8) < 0.05, "The dispatch-age qualification threshold is 51.8 ms.")
    # fig12_canonical_fallback_ladder.svg and parts/images/svg/fig_part3_record_chain.svg draw 1 kHz, 60 ms, and 51.6 ms from these guards.
    check(abs(tick.to(millisecond).magnitude - 1.0) < 1e-9, "The hand-drawn figures label the MCU tick 1 kHz.")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    chunk_rate_hz_str = fmt(chunk_rate.to(hertz).magnitude, precision=0)
    lease_ms_str = fmt_latency(lease, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    heartbeat_rate_hz_str = fmt(heartbeat_rate.to(hertz).magnitude, precision=0)
    heartbeat_timeout_ms_str = fmt_latency(heartbeat_timeout, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    self_watchdog_ms_str = fmt_latency(self_watchdog, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    tick_ms_str = fmt_latency(tick, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    tick_us_str = fmt_latency(tick, unit=microsecond, precision=0)
    loop_rate_str = fmt_frequency((1 / tick).to(hertz))
    bus_ms_str = fmt_latency(bus, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    onset_ms_str = fmt_latency(onset, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    renewal_to_onset_ms_str = fmt_latency(renewal_to_onset, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    t_age_str = fmt_latency(t_age, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
    eps_sync_str = fmt_latency(eps_sync, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
    age_threshold_str = fmt_latency(age_threshold, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
```

## The Tracker Handoff and Dynamic Reference Envelopes {#sec-enforcement-handoff}

The base can follow an admitted reference imperfectly even when every command arrives on time. The tracker, the feedback controller that turns each admitted reference into actuator effort (@sec-planning-handoff), must bound this difference over the maneuver. Its **worst-case tracking error tube** ($\epsilon_{\text{track}}$) bounds the departure of the tracked position output from its reference. In the tracking-error expressions here, $\mathbf{x}(t)$ and $\mathbf{r}(t)$ denote actual and reference positions in the same spatial coordinates, not a full state mixing position, velocity, and joint angle. A whole-body implementation instead needs a declared output map or weighted error metric that bounds the relevant swept-body displacement in meters. Enforcement needs that bound because clearance reserved around a reference must also contain the moving body.

Starting within the qualified initial-error region, and while reference velocity, acceleration, payload inertia, disturbances, and temperature remain inside their certified envelope, the closed-loop tracking stack guarantees the transient position-error bound:
$$\|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{r}(t)\| \le \epsilon_{\text{track}} \quad \forall t \ge 0.$$
The enforcer\index{Enforcer!tracking contract} uses the tracking layer's qualified error bound rather than reconstructing its controller design on each tick. That contract confines motion to the $\epsilon_{\text{track}}$\index{Tracking error bound} tube only while the conditions used to establish it remain true.

This bound is a physical distance dictated by reflected rotor inertia ($N^2 J$), transmission backlash, structural compliance, and actuator torque saturation\index{Actuator torque limits}. While a steady-state stiffness calculation balances constant external disturbances against closed-loop restoring force\index{Closed-loop stiffness}, it fails to bound transient overshoot or settling oscillations during aggressive maneuvers. The tracking tube bound $\epsilon_{\text{track}}$ must therefore be certified via full-envelope dynamic qualification testing.[^fn-math-tracking-error]

[^fn-math-tracking-error]: **Closed-loop tracking stiffness and disturbance bounds**\index{Tracking error!disturbance bounds}\index{Control loop!closed-loop stiffness}: Sustained force and effective closed-loop stiffness determine static deflection. Transient tracking also depends on inertia, damping, command shape, and saturation. Disturbances outside the validated envelope invalidate the claimed tube; they need not produce exponential divergence.

```{python}
#| label: calc-enforcement-tracking-bound
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ THE BASE'S TRACKING BOUND
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: the tracking-bound paragraphs immediately below.
# │ Goal:    state the inset the enforcer applies and what a doubled error costs.
# │ Show:    the base's tracking bound and the error if wear doubled it.
# │ How:     AISLE.eps_track, the same field row 7 of the stopping budget uses.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt_length, check

AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle

class EnforcementTrackingBound:
    # ┌── 1. LOAD ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    eps_track = AISLE.eps_track  # category: illustrative

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    eps_doubled = (2 * eps_track).to(millimeter)

    # ┌── 3. GUARD ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(eps_track.to(millimeter).magnitude - 40.0) < 1e-9, "The base's tracking bound is 40 mm.")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    eps_track_str = fmt_length(eps_track, unit=millimeter, precision=0)
    eps_doubled_str = fmt_length(eps_doubled, unit=millimeter, precision=0)
```

On the warehouse mobile manipulator's base, the illustrative full-maneuver qualification target is $\epsilon_{\text{track}} =$ `{python} EnforcementTrackingBound.eps_track_str` (illustrative; see the Reader Guide). The controller holds that bound only while three conditions hold. The reference cannot demand accelerations beyond what the drives can deliver, external disturbances must remain below $d_{\text{max}}$, and the actuators must operate below the continuous thermal derating limits of @sec-body-thermal-duty-cycles\index{Joule heating} and the limits of their voltage rail. A reference that demands more acceleration than peak torque allows saturates the loop\index{Actuator saturation}, so the base can fall behind the requested motion. Integral action can accumulate windup\index{Integrator windup} unless anti-windup limits it; the residual error depends on that controller and the duration of saturation. Outside the qualified envelope, this tracking certificate no longer supplies a bound, even if another controller analysis could establish one.

Because the physical base can lag its reference by up to $\epsilon_{\text{track}}$, a distance margin must reserve that error. Let $h$ measure the spatial clearance remaining around a reference. The contracted reference condition is:
$$h_{\text{contracted}}(\mathbf{r}) = h(\mathbf{r}) - \epsilon_{\text{track}} \ge 0.$$
A reference that keeps clearance $c$ from the rack end guarantees the base only $c - \epsilon_{\text{track}}$, so the enforcer checks the reference against the required clearance plus `{python} EnforcementTrackingBound.eps_track_str`, and @sec-enforcement-stopping-envelopes carries that inset into the stopping distance, where transport delay and localization error also consume clearance. If worn drive bearings, tire wear, or altered motor parameters doubled the true error to `{python} EnforcementTrackingBound.eps_doubled_str` without the record changing, the base would spend another `{python} EnforcementTrackingBound.eps_track_str` of clearance that the enforcer believes it still holds. A degraded tracking bound silently erodes every margin above it.

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↩ Spatial clearance insetting from sensor covariance and transport delay originates in @sec-perception-error-clearance.
:::

A tracking bound never checked at runtime is an assumption, not a contract. The Nervous System must publish $\epsilon_{\text{track}}$ with the operating conditions that validate it and monitor the instantaneous error $e(t) = \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{r}(t)\|$ on every millisecond tick. When $e(t)$ exceeds the bound—under a disturbance spike, sudden wheel slip, or thermal throttling—the contract has broken. The enforcer detects this violation, revokes the active admitted command, and selects a state-matched fallback. Containment still depends on the response remaining feasible after the tracking bound is lost.

::: {#psp-enforcement-inset-margin .callout-perspective title="The inset margin invariant"}
A spatial stopping boundary must reserve the tracking loop's qualified distance error. The stopping envelope of @eq-enforce-stopping-envelope carries that inset, together with travel during transport lag\index{Transport lag}, into admission. A barrier expressed in other units needs the corresponding bound on barrier change, rather than a distance subtracted directly. Evaluating barrier certificates\index{Barrier certificates} only on nominal geometry can admit a reference whose tracking tube intersects an obstacle.
:::

The synthesis of tracking controllers, observers, and disturbance rejection belongs to the control literature [@slotine1991applied; @astrom2021feedback]. A **cascaded control hierarchy**\index{Cascaded control!tracking architecture} turns position targets into velocity and current requests through nested feedback loops. A **tracking Model Predictive Controller (MPC)**\index{Model Predictive Control!tracking layer} instead computes corrective inputs over a short predicted horizon. Enforcement needs the resulting tracking bound whichever controller supplies it.

A tracker can accurately follow a reference that leads into a rack. Convergence to the reference therefore does not establish containment. Control Lyapunov functions formalize tracking convergence; their derivation and combination with hard barrier constraints are collected in @sec-appendix-control-lyapunov.

Tracking seeks the requested motion; enforcement decides whether that motion is admissible. The tracking bound enters that decision as the distance by which the body may differ from any reference the enforcer admits, and surface oil, a changed payload, or thermal current derating can widen it with the reference unchanged. The stopping envelope is where that distance is spent, together with every other term that stands between a moving base and the rack end.

## Stopping Envelopes {#sec-enforcement-stopping-envelopes}

The chapters that own a stopping term have each added it to the warehouse mobile manipulator's budget at the rack end, and the tracking inset completes the list of physical distance terms. The dispatch-to-admission interval still needs a qualified timing bound. The stopping envelope is the set of states from which a validated braking response can arrest motion before a boundary, and the irreversibility law (principle \ref{pri-vol4-irreversibility}) sets its test, $d_{\text{stop}} \le D_{\text{clear}}$ with every term tied to a limit and its evidence category. The running calculation uses illustrative limits; deployment requires their qualification on the actual machine. Reserving that response costs achievable speed, because velocity increases blind travel linearly and braking travel quadratically. The machine must remain inside this envelope before a fault or unsafe proposal occurs.

The pre-brake delay $\tau_{\text{delay}}$ in the stopping distance of @sec-body-kinetic-momentum already includes the enforcer's own permission-loop tick, which @sec-nervous-cadences budgets with the lease path. What remains is the gap between the reference and the plant that follows it.

The permission path closes that gap with the tracking bound $\epsilon_{\text{track}}$ of @sec-enforcement-handoff and defends the stopping distance of @eq-body-stopping-distance inset by it. A commanded reference can be admitted only if the plant, which may lag that reference by up to $\epsilon_{\text{track}}$, can still stop inside $D_{\text{clear}}$. The admission condition combines clearance and velocity into one test:
$$v\,\tau_{\text{delay}} + d_{\text{suffix}}(v) + \delta_{\text{loc}} + \delta_{\text{margin}} + \epsilon_{\text{track}} \le D_{\text{clear}}$$ {#eq-enforce-stopping-envelope}
Here $d_{\text{suffix}}(v)$ is the travel of the resident stop from speed $v$. It equals $v^2/2a_{\text{brake}}$ for constant-deceleration braking; for the jerk-limited stop of @sec-planning-behavior-seam it is @eq-plan-c2-stopping-suffix, which adds the travel of the jerk ramps; $\delta_{\text{loc}}$ is the localization bound and $\delta_{\text{margin}}$ the fixed protective clearance. The left side is the stopping distance $d_{\text{stop}}(v)$ of @eq-body-stopping-distance plus the tracking inset $\epsilon_{\text{track}}$.[^fn-math-stopping-dist]

[^fn-math-stopping-dist]: **Kinematic Stopping Distance**\index{Stopping envelope!kinematic distance}\index{Latency!stopping distance contribution}: The inset stopping distance in this model compounds five terms: blind travel, braking distance under the credible deceleration, the localization bound, the fixed protective clearance, and the transient tracking bound. Omitting computational transport delay or tracking error results in premature encroachment on physical obstacles before peak braking can engage. See @sec-appendix-systems-stopping for formal kinematic derivations.

The inequality defines a conditional stopping region. Within it, the modeled delay and resident braking response fit inside the available clearance. A state outside it lacks that stopping reservation under these assumptions; a conservative bound does not establish that collision is inevitable under every possible maneuver. Per-tick enforcement must preserve the reservation throughout the interval until the next command can take effect, not merely test the current position.

Under those delay, estimate, and braking assumptions, the enforcer refuses a proposal whose required distance in @eq-enforce-stopping-envelope exceeds the available clearance along the direction of travel. The stopping envelope is fundamentally anisotropic\index{Stopping envelope!Anisotropy}; direction changes which obstacles consume the braking reservation, while uncertainty and the body's swept motion still require clearance around the path.

### Sizing the composite stopping budget {#sec-enforcement-composite-budget}

The composite stopping budget joins the remaining distance claims into the **spatial footprint of the execution lease**. It reserves clearance for sensing age and software response, then for the resident stop and the gap between reference and body. Each term must describe the same operating conditions; otherwise their sum cannot justify admission.

```{python}
#| label: calc-enforcement-stopping-budget
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ THE FINISHED STOPPING BUDGET OF THE WAREHOUSE MOBILE MANIPULATOR
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: row 7 and aisle-speed prose below, @tbl-enforcement-stopping-budget.
# │ Goal:    add the tracking inset (row 7), then choose the aisle speed that the
# │          finished budget allows.
# │ Show:    each row's term, value, running total, and remainder at the drive
# │          limit; the same terms at the aisle speed; the ceiling; the time rows;
# │          the missed-tick cost reused by the cycle list; the walking-person
# │          ceiling (moved from @sec-memory-belief-through-occlusion); the
# │          base stall at the aisle speed (distance added, overrun past D_clear).
# │ How:     RM/AISLE fields; jerk bound = peak jerk of the reference C2
# │          polynomial at the drive limit (calc_c2_stop_suffix);
# │          calc_scurve_stop_distance / _time (row 6, stop rows);
# │          calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity (ceilings, solved numerically);
# │          calc_safe_stopping_distance with tau + a/(2j) (closed-form
# │          cross-check above a^2/j); RM.intent_inference_latency, the
# │          computed prefill-plus-decode latency (time row).
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
from mlsysim.physics.robotics import (
    calc_c2_stop_suffix,
    calc_scurve_stop_distance,
    calc_scurve_stop_time,
    calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity,
    calc_max_permitted_velocity,
    calc_safe_stopping_distance,
    calc_free_space_expiry,
)
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt, fmt_int, fmt_length, fmt_velocity, fmt_latency, fmt_acceleration, fmt_jerk, fmt_magnitude, fmt_math, check

RM = Embodied.MobileManipulator.WarehouseMobileManipulator
AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle

class EnforcementStoppingBudget:
    # ┌── 1. LOAD ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    v_drive = RM.base.max_velocity  # category: illustrative (drive limit)
    v_aisle = AISLE.v_aisle  # category: chosen
    a_brake = AISLE.a_brake  # category: illustrative (credible, loaded, dry floor)
    d_clear = AISLE.d_clear  # category: illustrative
    delta_loc = AISLE.delta_loc  # category: illustrative
    delta_margin = AISLE.delta_margin  # category: chosen
    eps_track = AISLE.eps_track  # category: illustrative
    t_act = AISLE.t_brake_onset  # category: illustrative
    t_lease = AISLE.t_lease  # category: chosen
    t_tick = AISLE.t_tick  # category: chosen
    t_bus = AISLE.t_bus  # category: illustrative
    t_age = AISLE.perception_age  # category: derived
    tau_delay = AISLE.tau_delay  # category: derived
    v_human = AISLE.v_human_approach  # category: datasheet (ISO 13855 K)
    mu_inspected = AISLE.mu_inspected_floor  # category: illustrative
    t_intent = RM.intent_inference_latency  # category: derived (deployed INT4 prefill plus decode, @sec-brain-memory-wall)
    t_stall = 200.0 * millisecond  # category: illustrative (proposer stall before any brake)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    lease_path = (t_lease + t_tick + t_bus).to(millisecond)
    overhead = (delta_loc + delta_margin).to(millimeter)
    # Jerk bound: the peak jerk of the reference C2 polynomial at the drive limit (@sec-planning-c2-stopping-suffix)
    j_brake = calc_c2_stop_suffix(v_drive, a_brake)["peak_jerk"].to(meter / second**3)
    v_plateau = (a_brake**2 / j_brake).to(meter / second)
    ramp_delay = (a_brake / (2 * j_brake)).to(millisecond)
    c2_drive = calc_scurve_stop_distance(v_drive, a_brake, j_brake).to(millimeter)
    c2_aisle = calc_scurve_stop_distance(v_aisle, a_brake, j_brake).to(millimeter)

    # Rows 1-7 at the drive limit, in book order
    brake_drive = (v_drive**2 / (2 * a_brake)).to(millimeter)
    onset_drive = (v_drive * t_act).to(millimeter)
    lease_drive = (v_drive * lease_path).to(millimeter)
    age_drive = (v_drive * t_age).to(millimeter)
    shape_drive = (c2_drive - brake_drive).to(millimeter)
    inset = eps_track.to(millimeter)
    run1 = brake_drive
    run2 = run1 + overhead
    run3 = run2 + onset_drive
    run4 = run3 + lease_drive
    run5 = run4 + age_drive
    run6 = run5 + shape_drive
    run7 = run6 + inset
    left = [
        (d_clear - run1).to(millimeter),
        (d_clear - run2).to(millimeter),
        (d_clear - run3).to(millimeter),
        (d_clear - run4).to(millimeter),
        (d_clear - run5).to(millimeter),
        (d_clear - run6).to(millimeter),
        (d_clear - run7).to(millimeter),
    ]

    # The same terms at the aisle speed
    brake_aisle = (v_aisle**2 / (2 * a_brake)).to(millimeter)
    onset_aisle = (v_aisle * t_act).to(millimeter)
    lease_aisle = (v_aisle * lease_path).to(millimeter)
    age_aisle = (v_aisle * t_age).to(millimeter)
    shape_aisle = (c2_aisle - brake_aisle).to(millimeter)
    total_aisle = (brake_aisle + overhead + onset_aisle + lease_aisle + age_aisle + shape_aisle + inset).to(millimeter)
    spare = (d_clear - total_aisle).to(millimeter)
    # Base stall: a last proposal that keeps authority for the stall instead of
    # the lease adds the extra delay's travel to the finished budget.
    stall_added = (v_aisle * (t_stall - t_lease)).to(millimeter)
    stall_breach = (total_aisle + stall_added - d_clear).to(millimeter)

    # Speed is the one free term: the ceiling of @eq-enforce-stopping-envelope
    ceiling = calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity(
        d_clear, tau_delay, a_brake, j_brake, loc_margin=delta_loc, physical_margin=delta_margin + eps_track
    ).to(meter / second)
    # Above a^2/j the S-curve is constant braking at a_brake with the delay lengthened by a/(2j)
    ceiling_closed = calc_max_permitted_velocity(
        d_clear, tau_delay + ramp_delay, a_brake, loc_margin=delta_loc, physical_margin=delta_margin + eps_track
    ).to(meter / second)
    total_check = calc_safe_stopping_distance(
        v_drive, tau_delay + ramp_delay, a_brake, loc_margin=delta_loc, physical_margin=delta_margin + eps_track
    ).to(millimeter)

    # Time rows (no distance added)
    # Free-space expiry abreast of the occluded rack end (@eq-mem-free-space-expiry):
    # the free depth is the hull-to-rack side clearance.
    belief_life = calc_free_space_expiry(AISLE.side_clearance, delta_loc, delta_margin, v_human).to(millisecond)
    missed_tick = (v_aisle * t_tick).to(millimeter)
    t_latest = (spare / v_aisle).to(millisecond)
    capture_to_admission_max = (t_age + t_latest).to(millisecond)
    capture_to_onset_max = (tau_delay + t_latest).to(millisecond)
    mu_min = (a_brake / ureg.standard_gravity).to("dimensionless").magnitude
    a_inspected = min(a_brake, (mu_inspected * ureg.standard_gravity).to(meter / second**2))
    # The floor caps the deceleration; the jerk bound belongs to the load and is unchanged.
    ceiling_inspected = calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity(
        d_clear, tau_delay, a_inspected, j_brake, loc_margin=delta_loc, physical_margin=delta_margin + eps_track
    ).to(meter / second)

    # Walking person: v tau + d_stop(v) + v_h (tau + T_stop(v)) + overhead = d_clear.
    # The S-curve's distance and time are not one polynomial in v, so MLSysIM solves it numerically.
    overhead_all = AISLE.fixed_overhead  # category: derived (delta_loc + delta_margin + eps_track)
    v_walk = calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity(
        d_clear, tau_delay, a_brake, j_brake, loc_margin=delta_loc, physical_margin=delta_margin + eps_track, approach_velocity=v_human
    ).to(meter / second)
    d_walk = (
        v_walk * tau_delay
        + calc_scurve_stop_distance(v_walk, a_brake, j_brake)
        + v_human * (tau_delay + calc_scurve_stop_time(v_walk, a_brake, j_brake))
        + overhead_all
    ).to(meter)
    # Why the walking-person ceiling is so low: below a^2/j the jerk-limited stop never
    # reaches a_brake and lasts 2 sqrt(v/j), far longer than v/a, and the person walks
    # for the whole stop.
    t_stop_walk = calc_scurve_stop_time(v_walk, a_brake, j_brake).to(millisecond)
    t_stop_walk_const = (v_walk / a_brake).to(millisecond)
    brake_walk = calc_scurve_stop_distance(v_walk, a_brake, j_brake).to(millimeter)
    closure_walk = (v_human * t_stop_walk).to(millimeter)
    # A reference polynomial rescaled to stop from v_walk at the full a_brake would need this jerk
    jerk_rescaled_walk = calc_c2_stop_suffix(v_walk, a_brake)["peak_jerk"].to(meter / second**3)
    # The same walking-person budget under constant-deceleration braking (no jerk bound):
    # v^2/2a + (tau + v_h/a) v + v_h tau + overhead - d_clear = 0, positive root
    _qa = 1 / (2 * a_brake)
    _qb = tau_delay + v_human / a_brake
    _qc = v_human * tau_delay + overhead_all - d_clear
    v_walk_const = ((-_qb + (_qb**2 - 4 * _qa * _qc) ** 0.5) / (2 * _qa)).to(meter / second)
    # Latency sensitivity of the static ceiling: 10 ms more pre-brake delay
    ceiling_plus10 = calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity(
        d_clear, tau_delay + 10 * millisecond, a_brake, j_brake, loc_margin=delta_loc, physical_margin=delta_margin + eps_track
    ).to(meter / second)
    ceiling_drop_10ms = (ceiling - ceiling_plus10).to(millimeter / second)

    # ┌── 3. GUARD ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(run1.magnitude - 562.5) < 1e-6, "Row 1 running total is 562.5 mm.")
    check(abs(run2.magnitude - 712.5) < 1e-6, "Row 2 running total is 712.5 mm.")
    check(abs(run3.magnitude - 742.5) < 1e-6, "Row 3 running total is 742.5 mm.")
    check(abs(run4.magnitude - 835.5) < 1e-6, "Row 4 running total is 835.5 mm.")
    check(abs(run5.magnitude - 912.9) < 1e-6, "Row 5 running total is 912.9 mm.")
    check(abs(j_brake.magnitude - 64.0 / 9.0) < 1e-9, "The jerk bound is the reference polynomial's 7.11 m/s^3 peak.")
    check(v_aisle >= v_plateau and v_drive >= v_plateau, "Both budget speeds reach the deceleration bound (trapezoidal regime).")
    check(abs(run6.magnitude - 1123.8375) < 1e-6, "Row 6 running total is 1123.84 mm.")
    check(abs(run7.magnitude - 1163.8375) < 1e-6, "Row 7 running total is 1163.84 mm.")
    check(abs(total_check.magnitude - run7.magnitude) < 1e-6, "Row 7 total must equal @eq-enforce-stopping-envelope at the drive limit.")
    check(abs(left[6].magnitude + 63.8375) < 1e-6, "Row 7 runs 63.84 mm past the clear distance.")
    check(abs(lease_path.magnitude - 62.0) < 1e-9, "Lease path is 62 ms.")
    check(abs(tau_delay.magnitude - 133.6) < 1e-9, "tau_delay is 133.6 ms.")
    check(abs(ceiling.magnitude - ceiling_closed.magnitude) < 1e-9, "Numerical ceiling must match the closed form above a^2/j.")
    check(ceiling >= v_plateau, "The ceiling lies in the trapezoidal regime.")
    check(abs(ceiling.magnitude - 1.4367) < 5e-5, "Ceiling is 1.44 m/s.")
    check(v_aisle < ceiling, "The chosen aisle speed must sit under the ceiling.")
    check(abs(total_aisle.magnitude - 968.9925) < 1e-6, "Budget at 1.3 m/s is 968.99 mm.")
    check(abs(spare.magnitude - 131.0075) < 1e-6, "Spare at 1.3 m/s is 131.01 mm.")
    check(abs(stall_added.magnitude - 182.0) < 1e-6, "A 200 ms stall adds 182 mm at 1.3 m/s.")
    check(stall_added > spare, "The stall's added travel exceeds the whole spare.")
    check(abs(stall_breach.magnitude - 50.9925) < 5e-3, "The stall runs 51.0 mm past the clear distance.")
    # 2026-09-28 (M1/M2): the deployed intent model is INT4; its full computed inference replaces the FP16 weight sweep.
    check(abs(t_intent.to(millisecond).magnitude - 335.61) < 5e-3, f"Intent inference latency drifted: {t_intent}")
    check(t_intent > t_lease, "The intent inference cannot renew a chunk lease.")
    check(belief_life.magnitude == 0.0, "Abreast of the occluded rack end the free-space claim expires at capture.")
    check(abs(missed_tick.magnitude - 1.3) < 1e-9, "One missed tick costs 1.3 mm at 1.3 m/s.")
    check(abs(t_latest.magnitude - 100.775) < 5e-3, "The unallocated timing allowance is 100.8 ms at 1.3 m/s.")
    check(
        abs((capture_to_onset_max - capture_to_admission_max - t_lease - t_tick - t_bus - t_act).to(millisecond).magnitude) < 1e-9,
        "Admission-to-onset must contain the lease, tick, bus, and drive onset exactly once.",
    )
    check(abs(mu_min - 0.204) < 5e-4, "Friction premise is 0.204.")
    check(abs(ceiling_inspected.magnitude - 1.2309) < 5e-5, "Inspected-floor ceiling is 1.23 m/s.")
    check(abs(v_walk.magnitude - 0.2599) < 5e-5, f"Walking-person ceiling should be 0.260 m/s, got {v_walk}.")
    check(v_walk < v_plateau, "The walking-person stop never reaches the deceleration bound.")
    check(abs((d_walk - d_clear).to(millimeter).magnitude) < 1e-6, "At the walking-person ceiling the budget must fill the clear distance exactly.")
    check(abs(t_stop_walk.magnitude - 382.38) < 5e-2, "The jerk-limited stop from the walking-person ceiling lasts about 382 ms.")
    check(t_stop_walk > 2.9 * t_stop_walk_const, "Below a^2/j the jerk-limited stop lasts roughly three times a constant-deceleration stop.")
    check(closure_walk > 10 * brake_walk, "The person closes more than ten times the base's own braking travel.")
    check(jerk_rescaled_walk > 5 * j_brake, "Reaching a_brake from the walking-person ceiling would need several times the jerk bound.")
    check(abs(v_walk_const.magnitude - 0.6371) < 5e-4, "Without the jerk bound the walking-person ceiling would be 0.64 m/s.")
    check(ceiling_drop_10ms.magnitude > 0, "More pre-brake delay must lower the ceiling.")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    v_drive_str = fmt_velocity(v_drive, precision=1)
    v_aisle_str = fmt_velocity(v_aisle, precision=1)
    ceiling_str = fmt_velocity(ceiling, precision=2)
    ceiling_inspected_str = fmt_velocity(ceiling_inspected, precision=2)
    v_walk_str = fmt_velocity(v_walk, precision=2)
    v_plateau_str = fmt_velocity(v_plateau, precision=2)
    v_human_str = fmt_velocity(v_human, precision=1)
    t_stop_walk_str = fmt_latency(round(t_stop_walk.magnitude) * millisecond, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    t_stop_walk_const_str = fmt_latency(round(t_stop_walk_const.magnitude) * millisecond, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    brake_walk_str = fmt_length(round(brake_walk.magnitude) * millimeter, unit=millimeter, precision=0)
    closure_walk_str = fmt_length(round(closure_walk.magnitude) * millimeter, unit=millimeter, precision=0)
    jerk_rescaled_walk_str = fmt_jerk(round(jerk_rescaled_walk.magnitude) * meter / second**3, precision=0)
    v_walk_const_str = fmt_velocity(v_walk_const, precision=2)
    ceiling_drop_10ms_str = fmt_int(ceiling_drop_10ms.magnitude)
    d_clear_str = fmt_length(d_clear, unit=meter, precision=2)
    a_brake_str = fmt_acceleration(a_brake, precision=0)
    j_brake_str = fmt_jerk(j_brake, precision=2)
    ramp_delay_str = fmt_latency(ramp_delay, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
    tau_delay_str = fmt_latency(tau_delay, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
    lease_path_str = fmt_latency(lease_path, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    t_age_str = fmt_latency(t_age, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
    t_intent_str = fmt_latency(round(t_intent.to(millisecond).magnitude) * millisecond, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    belief_life_str = fmt_latency(belief_life, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    missed_tick_str = fmt_length(missed_tick, unit=millimeter, precision=1)
    t_latest_str = fmt_latency(t_latest, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
    capture_to_admission_max_str = fmt_latency(capture_to_admission_max, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
    capture_to_onset_max_str = fmt_latency(capture_to_onset_max, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
    mu_min_str = fmt(mu_min, precision=3)
    mu_inspected_str = fmt(mu_inspected, precision=2)
    inset_str = fmt_length(inset, unit=millimeter, precision=0)
    run6_str = fmt_length(run6, unit=millimeter, precision=2)
    run7_str = fmt_length(run7, unit=millimeter, precision=2)
    over7_str = fmt_length(-left[6], unit=millimeter, precision=2)
    total_aisle_str = fmt_length(total_aisle, unit=millimeter, precision=1)
    spare_str = fmt_length(spare, unit=millimeter, precision=1)
    t_stall_str = fmt_latency(t_stall, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    stall_added_str = fmt_length(stall_added, unit=millimeter, precision=0)
    stall_breach_str = fmt_length(stall_breach, unit=millimeter, precision=2)
    # Table cells (the column headers carry mm)
    brake_drive_value_str = fmt_magnitude(brake_drive, millimeter, precision=1, commas=True)
    overhead_value_str = fmt_magnitude(overhead, millimeter, precision=0, commas=True)
    onset_drive_value_str = fmt_magnitude(onset_drive, millimeter, precision=0, commas=True)
    lease_drive_value_str = fmt_magnitude(lease_drive, millimeter, precision=0, commas=True)
    age_drive_value_str = fmt_magnitude(age_drive, millimeter, precision=1, commas=True)
    shape_drive_value_str = fmt_magnitude(shape_drive, millimeter, precision=2, commas=True)
    inset_value_str = fmt_magnitude(inset, millimeter, precision=0, commas=True)
    run1_value_str = fmt_magnitude(run1, millimeter, precision=1, commas=True)
    run2_value_str = fmt_magnitude(run2, millimeter, precision=1, commas=True)
    run3_value_str = fmt_magnitude(run3, millimeter, precision=1, commas=True)
    run4_value_str = fmt_magnitude(run4, millimeter, precision=1, commas=True)
    run5_value_str = fmt_magnitude(run5, millimeter, precision=1, commas=True)
    run6_value_str = fmt_magnitude(run6, millimeter, precision=2, commas=True)
    run7_value_str = fmt_magnitude(run7, millimeter, precision=2, commas=True)
    left1_value_str = fmt_magnitude(left[0], millimeter, precision=1, commas=True)
    left2_value_str = fmt_magnitude(left[1], millimeter, precision=1, commas=True)
    left3_value_str = fmt_magnitude(left[2], millimeter, precision=1, commas=True)
    left4_value_str = fmt_magnitude(left[3], millimeter, precision=1, commas=True)
    left5_value_str = fmt_magnitude(left[4], millimeter, precision=1, commas=True)
    left6_math = fmt_math(fmt_magnitude(left[5], millimeter, precision=2, commas=True))
    left7_math = fmt_math(fmt_magnitude(left[6], millimeter, precision=2, commas=True))
    brake_aisle_value_str = fmt_magnitude(brake_aisle, millimeter, precision=1, commas=True)
    onset_aisle_value_str = fmt_magnitude(onset_aisle, millimeter, precision=0, commas=True)
    lease_aisle_value_str = fmt_magnitude(lease_aisle, millimeter, precision=1, commas=True)
    age_aisle_value_str = fmt_magnitude(age_aisle, millimeter, precision=2, commas=True)
    shape_aisle_value_str = fmt_magnitude(shape_aisle, millimeter, precision=2, commas=True)
    total_aisle_value_str = fmt_magnitude(total_aisle, millimeter, precision=2, commas=True)
    spare_value_str = fmt_magnitude(spare, millimeter, precision=2, commas=True)
```

For the warehouse mobile manipulator, the inset is the base's tracking bound of `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.inset_str`, and it is the last distance term the budget receives. At the `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.v_drive_str` drive limit, the matched stop suffix of @sec-planning-behavior-seam had already carried the running total to `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.run6_str`, past the `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.d_clear_str` clear distance at the rack end. The inset brings it to `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.run7_str`, `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.over7_str` more than the clear distance.

The accounted terms in @eq-enforce-stopping-envelope come from the chapters that own them: the credible deceleration and the fixed overheads by @sec-body-kinetic-momentum, the lease path by @sec-nervous-cadences, the observation age by @sec-perception-transduction-calibration, the stop's shape by @sec-planning-behavior-seam, and the inset here. The $C^2$ stop suffix replaces constant deceleration ($v^2 / 2a_{\text{brake}}$) with jerk-limited S-curve braking at the same peak and a jerk bound of $j_{\max} =$ `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.j_brake_str`. Both budget speeds reach the deceleration bound, so by @eq-plan-c2-stopping-suffix the stop adds the travel of half a jerk ramp:
$$d_{\text{suffix}}(v) = \frac{v^2}{2 a_{\text{brake}}} + v\,\frac{a_{\text{brake}}}{2 j_{\max}}.$$
The shaped stop spends more clearance than constant-deceleration braking, so the admissible speed must be solved from the finished budget.

Speed is the one term the machine can still choose. With the currently accounted delay $\tau_{\text{delay}} =$ `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.tau_delay_str`, the jerk ramps act as `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.ramp_delay_str` of extra delay before braking at $a_{\text{brake}}$, so the ceiling is the positive root of a quadratic, `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.ceiling_str`. Below $a_{\text{brake}}^2/j_{\max}$ the stop never reaches $a_{\text{brake}}$ and its distance is no longer quadratic in $v$; MLSysIM then solves @eq-enforce-stopping-envelope numerically. We select `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.v_aisle_str` as a candidate below that ceiling. The listed terms then total `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.total_aisle_str`, leaving `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.spare_str` before any unaccounted delay or additional reserve.

That remainder is small against the failures it must absorb. Were the chunk lease left to the host to honor, a last proposal that kept its authority for `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.t_stall_str` instead of the `{python} EnforcementLeaseStop.lease_ms_str` lease would add `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.stall_added_str` to the stop and carry the base `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.stall_breach_str` past the clear distance at the rack end, which is why the MCU enforces the lease itself (@sec-enforcement-authority-refuse).

The observation-age term ends at dispatch, whereas the execution lease begins at admission. Let $\Delta_{\text{da}}$ denote elapsed dispatch-to-admission time not already charged in the listed intervals. The complete delay is $\tau_{\mathrm{true}}=\tau_{\text{delay}}+\Delta_{\text{da}}$, and the actual reservation adds $v\Delta_{\text{da}}$ to the table's subtotal. This interval includes any remaining inference, admission work, and waiting on that path; overlapping stages must not be charged twice. A refreshed observation can change the ledger only if the implementation actually supplies and qualifies it before activation. @Fig-12-capture-to-onset lays these intervals end to end on one time axis and reads the same axis as travel at the aisle speed.

At the candidate speed, the entire unallocated allowance corresponds to `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.t_latest_str`. Equivalently, capture-to-admission must remain below `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.capture_to_admission_max_str` and capture-to-braking-onset below `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.capture_to_onset_max_str` to leave positive reserve under these assumptions. Equality spends all the remaining clearance. These are requirements to qualify, not measured achievements. Thus the calculation supports a useful design choice and a concrete timing acceptance test; it does not yet close permission for that speed. @Tbl-enforcement-stopping-budget and @fig-enforcement-stopping-budget show the accounted terms from which that test follows.

: **The warehouse mobile manipulator's stopping budget**: Each numbered row is the distance one chapter adds, loaded and on a dry floor, at the `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.v_drive_str` drive limit and at the `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.v_aisle_str` aisle speed; the running total and remainder are at the drive limit, against the `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.d_clear_str` clear distance. Row 6 replaces constant-deceleration braking with the resident jerk-limited $C^2$ stop, so its entry is the added distance. Time rows add no distance. The totals exclude unaccounted dispatch-to-admission travel, which must be charged before activation. {#tbl-enforcement-stopping-budget tbl-colwidths="[5,17,38,10,10,10,10]"}

::: {#fig-enforcement-stopping-budget fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**The stopping budget, row by row**: Each bar is the running total after one chapter adds its term, at the drive limit, loaded, on a dry floor. Braking, overhead, brake onset, the lease path, and the observation age stay inside the clear distance; the matched stop suffix carries the total past it, and the tracking inset widens the overrun. The final bar is the accounted subtotal at the candidate aisle speed. Its remainder must first cover unaccounted dispatch-to-admission travel; only the balance is available for further reserve." fig-alt="Stacked bar chart of stopping distance in millimeters. Seven bars at the drive limit grow from braking alone to the full budget, adding overhead, brake onset, lease path, observation age, the matched stop suffix, and the tracking inset; the sixth and seventh bars cross a dashed horizontal line marking the clear distance at the rack end. An eighth bar at the aisle speed, built from the same terms, ends below the line."}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ THE STOPPING BUDGET, ROW BY ROW (FIGURE)
# │ Context: @fig-enforcement-stopping-budget
# │ Goal:    show each chapter's term accumulating against the clear distance
# │ Show:    seven stacked bars at the drive limit, one at the aisle speed,
# │          and the clear-distance line
# │ How:     the terms of @tbl-enforcement-stopping-budget from RM/AISLE
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.physics.robotics import calc_c2_stop_suffix, calc_scurve_stop_distance
from mlsysim.fmt import check
from mlsysim import viz

RM = Embodied.MobileManipulator.WarehouseMobileManipulator
AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle

# ┌── 1. LOAD ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
v_drive = RM.base.max_velocity  # category: illustrative (drive limit)
v_aisle = AISLE.v_aisle  # category: chosen
a_brake = AISLE.a_brake  # category: illustrative
j_brake = calc_c2_stop_suffix(v_drive, a_brake)["peak_jerk"]  # category: derived (reference polynomial's peak jerk)
lease_path = AISLE.t_lease + AISLE.t_tick + AISLE.t_bus  # category: chosen (lease, tick) + illustrative (bus)
d_clear_mm = AISLE.d_clear.to(millimeter).magnitude  # category: illustrative

# ┌── 2. EXECUTE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def terms(v):
    brake = (v**2 / (2 * a_brake)).to(millimeter).magnitude
    c2 = calc_scurve_stop_distance(v, a_brake, j_brake).to(millimeter).magnitude
    return {
        "braking": brake,
        "overhead": (AISLE.delta_loc + AISLE.delta_margin).to(millimeter).magnitude,
        "brake onset": (v * AISLE.t_brake_onset).to(millimeter).magnitude,
        "lease path": (v * lease_path).to(millimeter).magnitude,
        "observation age": (v * AISLE.perception_age).to(millimeter).magnitude,
        "stop-suffix shape": c2 - brake,
        "tracking inset": AISLE.eps_track.to(millimeter).magnitude,
    }

order = list(terms(v_drive).keys())
drive = terms(v_drive)
aisle = terms(v_aisle)
bars = [{k: (drive[k] if i <= n else 0.0) for i, k in enumerate(order)} for n in range(len(order))]
bars.append(aisle)
totals = [sum(b.values()) for b in bars]

# ┌── 3. GUARD ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
check(abs(totals[6] - 1163.8375) < 1e-6, "Row 7 total at the drive limit is 1163.84 mm.")
check(abs(totals[7] - 968.9925) < 1e-6, "The aisle-speed bar is 968.99 mm.")
check(totals[4] < d_clear_mm < totals[5], "The budget first passes the clear distance at row 6.")

# ┌── 4. PLOT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax, COLORS, plt = viz.setup_plot(figsize=(8, 4.6))
palette = {
    "braking": COLORS["BlueLine"],
    "overhead": COLORS["grid"],
    "brake onset": COLORS["BrownLine"],
    "lease path": COLORS["VioletLine"],
    "observation age": COLORS["OrangeLine"],
    "stop-suffix shape": COLORS["BlueL"],
    "tracking inset": COLORS["GreenLine"],
}
labels = [
    "1\nbraking",
    "2\n+ overhead",
    "3\n+ onset",
    "4\n+ lease",
    "5\n+ age",
    "6\n+ $C^2$ stop",
    "7\n+ inset",
    f"aisle\n{v_aisle.to(meter / second).magnitude:.1f} m/s",
]
x = list(range(len(bars)))
bottoms = [0.0] * len(bars)
for k in order:
    heights = [b[k] for b in bars]
    ax.bar(x, heights, bottom=bottoms, width=0.66, color=palette[k], edgecolor="white", lw=0.6, label=k, zorder=3)
    bottoms = [bt + h for bt, h in zip(bottoms, heights)]
for xi, t in zip(x, totals):
    ax.text(xi, t + 18, f"{t:,.2f}".rstrip("0").rstrip("."), ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8.5, color=COLORS["primary"], zorder=5)

ax.axhline(d_clear_mm, color=COLORS["RedLine"], lw=1.4, ls=(0, (5, 3)), zorder=4)
ax.text(
    -0.45,
    d_clear_mm + 18,
    f"clear distance at the rack end, {d_clear_mm:,.0f} mm",
    color=COLORS["RedLine"],
    fontsize=8.5,
    ha="left",
    va="bottom",
    zorder=5,
)
ax.axvline(6.5, color=COLORS["grid"], lw=0.8, zorder=2)
ax.text(3.0, 1440, f"drive limit, {v_drive.to(meter / second).magnitude:.1f} m/s", fontsize=8.5, color=COLORS["primary"], ha="center", va="bottom")

ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=8.5)
ax.set_xlim(-0.6, len(bars) - 0.4)
ax.set_ylim(0, 1520)
ax.set_ylabel("Stopping distance (mm)")
handles, leg_labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax.legend(handles[::-1], leg_labels[::-1], loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1.0), fontsize=8.5, frameon=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

:::

::: {#fig-12-capture-to-onset fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**From capture to brake onset, in time and in travel**: The warehouse mobile manipulator's permission path at the `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.v_aisle_str` aisle speed, drawn to scale from the exposure midpoint of the frame that first shows the hazard. The observation age of `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.t_age_str` ends at dispatch; the hatched dispatch-to-admission interval is the allocation @sec-placement makes, not a qualified bound; the lease, one tick, one bus cycle, and drive onset follow admission. The row beneath reads the same axis as travel, so the `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.t_latest_str` timing allowance and the `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.spare_str` spare are one interval. Admission later than `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.capture_to_admission_max_str`, or onset later than `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.capture_to_onset_max_str`, spends clearance the budget does not have. The jerk-limited stop that follows onset runs past the right edge." fig-alt="Timing strip with five lanes labeled camera, perception, proposal, permission, and drive over a time axis in milliseconds. Exposure and readout bars start the camera lane, an observation-age bar ends at a dispatch marker, a hatched dispatch-to-admission bar ends at an admission marker, a lease bar ends at lease expiry followed by a short tick and bus bar, and a drive-onset bar ends at brake onset, after which a solid stop bar runs off the right edge. A bracket over the strip marks the timing allowance from dispatch to a dashed latest-admission line; a second dashed line marks the latest onset. A travel row beneath converts the axis to millimeters and brackets the same interval as the spare distance."}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ CAPTURE TO BRAKE ONSET (TIMING STRIP FIGURE)
# │ Context: @fig-12-capture-to-onset
# │ Goal:    show the permission path as time becoming distance, with the
# │          unallocated timing allowance and the spare as one interval
# │ Show:    exposure, readout, observation age, Delta_da (hatched), lease,
# │          tick, bus, onset, the jerk-limited stop; the allowance bracket and
# │          the latest admission and onset; travel at the aisle speed
# │ How:     viz.capture_to_onset_strip reads every duration from AISLE
# │          (Delta_da = AISLE.t_dispatch_to_admission); the allowance and the
# │          spare come from EnforcementStoppingBudget; the stop from
# │          calc_scurve_stop_time / _distance at the aisle speed
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.physics.robotics import calc_scurve_stop_distance, calc_scurve_stop_time
from mlsysim.fmt import check
from mlsysim import viz
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle
S = EnforcementStoppingBudget

# ┌── 1. LOAD ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
v_aisle = S.v_aisle  # category: chosen
t_allow = S.t_latest  # category: derived (spare / v at the aisle speed)
spare = S.spare  # category: derived
t_stop = calc_scurve_stop_time(v_aisle, S.a_brake, S.j_brake)  # category: derived
d_stop = calc_scurve_stop_distance(v_aisle, S.a_brake, S.j_brake)  # category: derived

# ┌── 2. EXECUTE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
strip = viz.capture_to_onset_strip(AISLE, v_aisle, t_allowance=t_allow, spare=spare, stop_time=t_stop, stop_distance=d_stop, xlim=(-14, 262))
t_latest_adm = next(e.t for e in strip.events if e.label.startswith("latest admission"))
t_latest_onset = next(e.t for e in strip.events if e.label.startswith("latest onset"))

# ┌── 3. GUARD ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
check(abs(t_latest_adm - S.capture_to_admission_max.to(millisecond).magnitude) < 1e-9, "The strip's latest admission must match the budget cell.")
check(abs(t_latest_onset - S.capture_to_onset_max.to(millisecond).magnitude) < 1e-9, "The strip's latest onset must match the budget cell.")
check(AISLE.t_dispatch_to_admission < t_allow, "The allocated Delta_da must fit inside the timing allowance.")
check(
    abs((spare / v_aisle).to(millisecond).magnitude - t_allow.to(millisecond).magnitude) < 1e-9,
    "The allowance and the spare are one interval at the aisle speed.",
)

# ┌── 4. PLOT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax, axd = viz.plot_timing_strip(strip)
plt.show()
```

:::

The stopping model addresses a static obstacle at $D_{\text{clear}}$, such as a person who has stepped out from the rack and stopped or a dropped tote, so it assumes that the obstacle stays where it was when the stop began. A person who keeps walking toward the base through the whole stop closes the gap from the far side as well (@sec-memory-belief-through-occlusion), and counting that approach on top of the accounted terms would cap the base at `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.v_walk_str` at this rack end.

The ceiling is this low because a moving obstacle charges the stop by its duration, not its distance. The person approaches at $v_h =$ `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.v_human_str` throughout $\tau_{\text{delay}} + T_{\text{stop}}(v)$, so the budget gains a term $v_h\,T_{\text{stop}}(v)$ that the static case never carried. Below $a_{\text{brake}}^2/j_{\max} =$ `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.v_plateau_str` the jerk-limited stop never reaches $a_{\text{brake}}$: it ramps deceleration up and straight back down, and its duration is $2\sqrt{v/j_{\max}}$, which shrinks far more slowly than $v/a_{\text{brake}}$ as speed falls. From `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.v_walk_str` the stop lasts `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.t_stop_walk_str`, against `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.t_stop_walk_const_str` for a constant-deceleration stop. The base itself travels only `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.brake_walk_str` while braking, but the person closes `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.closure_walk_str` in that time. Reaching the full deceleration from so low a speed would take a jerk of `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.jerk_rescaled_walk_str`, several times the bound the load is qualified for, and constant-deceleration braking with no jerk bound would allow `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.v_walk_const_str`. The jerk bound therefore costs little clearance at aisle speed and a large share of it at walking pace, which is why slowing down helps much less against a moving person than against a static obstacle.

An aisle held to the walking-person ceiling would slow every run for an encounter that a crossing rule can keep out of the stop, so the selected operating concept requires an enforced crossing restriction, and @sec-frontier-residual-claims-register keeps open the premise the rule rests on, that no person approaches the rack end during a stop. Until the crossing restriction has supporting evidence, the faster operating mode remains a candidate. This calculation supports a static-obstacle stopping claim; it does not establish protection against a person who continues approaching.

Later decisions can spend only the reserve left after dispatch-to-admission travel is charged, so takeover waiting in @sec-intervention-authority-transitions cannot claim the `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.t_latest_str` allowance a second time. The credible deceleration binds only on floors with friction of at least `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.mu_min_str`, since $a=\min(a_{\text{brake}},\mu g)$, so on a floor inspected to `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.mu_inspected_str` the ceiling falls to `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.ceiling_inspected_str` (@sec-frontier-residual-claims-register). @Fig-12-stopping-vs-speed places the dry-floor, inspected-floor, and walking-person ceilings on one speed axis.

::: {#fig-12-stopping-vs-speed fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**Stopping distance against speed, and the three ceilings**: The stacked bands build the dry-floor stop from the fixed allowances, the travel during the `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.tau_delay_str` pre-brake delay, constant-deceleration braking, and the extra travel of the jerk ramps. Delay travel grows linearly with speed and braking travel quadratically, so the total meets the `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.d_clear_str` clear distance at `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.ceiling_str`. The dashed curve lowers the deceleration to what a floor inspected to $\mu =$ `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.mu_inspected_str` supports, moving the ceiling to `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.ceiling_inspected_str`. The dotted curve adds the closure of a person walking toward the base through the delay and the stop, which charges the stop by its duration and caps speed at `{python} EnforcementStoppingBudget.v_walk_str`." fig-alt="Plot of stopping distance in millimeters against speed in meters per second. Four stacked bands, a flat band of fixed allowances, a linearly growing band of delay travel, a quadratic braking band, and a thin band of jerk-ramp travel, rise to a solid total curve. A dashed curve for a low-friction floor and a dotted curve for a walking person rise more steeply. A dashed horizontal line marks the clear distance, and three markers where the curves cross it are labeled with their speed ceilings."}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ STOPPING DISTANCE AGAINST SPEED (FIGURE)
# │ Context: @fig-12-stopping-vs-speed
# │ Goal:    show why speed, not delay, is the free term, and how floor and a
# │          walking person move the ceiling
# │ Show:    fixed allowances, v tau_delay, v^2/2a, the S-curve's jerk-ramp
# │          travel; the inspected-floor and walking-person totals; D_clear;
# │          the three ceilings
# │ How:     calc_scurve_stop_distance / _time over a speed grid with the
# │          EnforcementStoppingBudget inputs (a_brake, j_brake, tau_delay,
# │          overheads, v_h, inspected-floor deceleration); ceilings read from
# │          the budget cell and guarded against the plotted crossings
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import numpy as np
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.physics.robotics import calc_scurve_stop_distance, calc_scurve_stop_time
from mlsysim.fmt import check
from mlsysim import viz

AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle
S = EnforcementStoppingBudget
MPS = meter / second

# ┌── 1. LOAD ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
tau = S.tau_delay.to(second).magnitude  # category: derived
fixed = AISLE.fixed_overhead.to(millimeter).magnitude  # category: derived (delta_loc + delta_margin + eps_track)
d_clear = S.d_clear.to(millimeter).magnitude  # category: illustrative
v_h = S.v_human.to(MPS).magnitude  # category: datasheet (ISO 13855 K)
v_drive = S.v_drive.to(MPS).magnitude  # category: illustrative (drive limit)
ceilings = {  # category: derived (budget cell)
    "dry": S.ceiling.to(MPS).magnitude,
    "inspected": S.ceiling_inspected.to(MPS).magnitude,
    "walking": S.v_walk.to(MPS).magnitude,
}

# ┌── 2. EXECUTE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def d_s(v, a):
    return calc_scurve_stop_distance(v * MPS, a, S.j_brake).to(millimeter).magnitude

def t_s(v, a):
    return calc_scurve_stop_time(v * MPS, a, S.j_brake).to(second).magnitude

a_dry = S.a_brake.to(meter / second**2).magnitude
v = np.linspace(0.0, 1.6, 321)
delay = v * tau * 1000.0
braking = v**2 / (2 * a_dry) * 1000.0
ramps = np.array([d_s(x, S.a_brake) for x in v]) - braking
total = fixed + delay + braking + ramps
total_inspected = fixed + delay + np.array([d_s(x, S.a_inspected) for x in v])
total_walking = total + v_h * (tau + np.array([t_s(x, S.a_brake) for x in v])) * 1000.0

def total_at(x, case):
    if case == "dry":
        return fixed + x * tau * 1000 + d_s(x, S.a_brake)
    if case == "inspected":
        return fixed + x * tau * 1000 + d_s(x, S.a_inspected)
    return fixed + x * tau * 1000 + d_s(x, S.a_brake) + v_h * (tau + t_s(x, S.a_brake)) * 1000

# ┌── 3. GUARD ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
for case, vc in ceilings.items():
    check(abs(total_at(vc, case) - d_clear) < 1e-3, f"The {case} curve must meet D_clear at its ceiling.")
check(ceilings["walking"] < ceilings["inspected"] < ceilings["dry"] < v_drive, "Ceiling order: walking < inspected < dry < drive limit.")
check(np.all(ramps >= -1e-9), "The jerk-limited stop never travels less than constant-deceleration braking.")

# ┌── 4. PLOT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax, COLORS, plt = viz.setup_plot(figsize=(10, 4.6))
base = np.full_like(v, fixed)
ax.fill_between(v, 0, base, color=COLORS["grid"], alpha=0.7, lw=0, label="fixed allowances", zorder=2)
ax.fill_between(v, base, base + delay, color=COLORS["BrownL"], lw=0, label="pre-brake delay travel", zorder=2)
ax.fill_between(v, base + delay, base + delay + braking, color=COLORS["BlueLine"], alpha=0.85, lw=0, label="constant-deceleration braking", zorder=2)
ax.fill_between(v, base + delay + braking, total, color=COLORS["BlueL"], lw=0, label="jerk-ramp travel", zorder=2)
ax.plot(v, total, color=COLORS["primary"], lw=1.6, label="total, dry floor", zorder=4)
ax.plot(v, total_inspected, color=COLORS["primary"], lw=1.4, ls=(0, (5, 3)), label="total, inspected floor", zorder=4)
ax.plot(v, total_walking, color=COLORS["primary"], lw=1.4, ls=(0, (1, 1.6)), label="total, person walking in", zorder=4)
ax.axhline(d_clear, color=COLORS["RedLine"], lw=1.3, ls=(0, (6, 3)), zorder=3)
ax.text(
    0.62,
    d_clear - 25,
    f"clear distance {d_clear / 1000:.2f} m",
    color=COLORS["RedLine"],
    fontsize=9,
    va="top",
    bbox=dict(boxstyle="square,pad=0.1", fc="white", ec="none"),
    zorder=5,
)

# label offsets (dx in m/s, dy in mm, alignment): kept inside the axes and off the legend
offsets = {"walking": (0.08, 180, "left"), "inspected": (-0.08, 220, "right"), "dry": (0.12, 620, "right")}
for case, vc in ceilings.items():
    ax.plot([vc], [d_clear], "o", ms=6, mfc="white", mec=COLORS["RedLine"], mew=1.5, zorder=6)
    ax.vlines(vc, 0, d_clear, color=COLORS["RedLine"], lw=0.8, ls=(0, (1, 2)), zorder=3)
    dx, dy, ha = offsets[case]
    ax.annotate(
        f"{case}: {vc:.2f} m/s",
        xy=(vc, d_clear),
        xytext=(vc + dx, d_clear + dy),
        fontsize=9,
        ha=ha,
        color=COLORS["RedLine"],
        arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=COLORS["RedLine"], lw=0.8),
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="square,pad=0.1", fc="white", ec="none"),
        zorder=6,
    )

ax.set_xlim(0, 1.6)
ax.set_ylim(0, 1800)
ax.set_xlabel("Speed at the start of the delay, $v$ (m/s)")
ax.set_ylabel("Stopping distance (mm)")
# legend outside the axes: inside, the walking-person curve and the clear-distance label run under it
ax.legend(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1.0), fontsize=8.5, frameon=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

:::

An independent protective scanner needs its own event-to-stop ledger. Its detection, safety-output, controller, communication, and drive-onset delays replace the vision-dispatch and proposal-lease intervals when its protective response bypasses them. The response still reserves the appropriate braking travel, tracking error, localization uncertainty, and protective margin; only intervals actually traversed belong in its sum. A mobile base can use a risk-assessed protective field under applicable vehicle and machinery standards, including ISO 3691-4 [@iso3691part4] and ISO 13849-1 [@iso13849part1], such as the scanner in @fig-12-real-laser-scanner. The field length follows that scanner path's qualified ledger, not an automatic reuse of the proposal path's lease and vision delays. The scanner is a certified safety device in its own right, separate from the perception LiDAR, whose range feeds the proposal and admission paths but carries no safety rating. On a certified machine this scanner path, not the vision path, carries the claim for a person at the rack end. @Sec-enforcement-certified-functions places the vision-path budget above that certified floor and shows that the vehicle standard tests person detection against the same static-obstacle convention the budget uses.

::: {#fig-12-real-laser-scanner fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**Planar laser scanner**: A rotating mirror sweeps a time-of-flight beam across a horizontal fan, so the device reports range over one plane around the base. A safety-rated scanner of this form adds an early warning field and a protective field. The warning field requests earlier deceleration; the protective field's safety output feeds a controller that selects a risk-assessed stop. Protective-field length must include scanner response, controller and drive delay, braking travel, and uncertainty; a moving base does not become safe merely because motor torque is removed. (Photograph: [Björn Heller](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sick_laserscanner.jpg) / Wikimedia Commons, [CC BY-SA 3.0 DE](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/de/deed.en).)" fig-alt="Photograph of a blue industrial laser scanner on an office desk beside a keyboard and mouse. A boxy upper housing carries a small status window and the maker's label; below it a black cylindrical window wraps around the base, behind which the beam sweeps."}
![](images/jpg/fig12_real_laser_scanner.jpg){width="85%"}
:::

### Dynamic phase portraits and speed ceilings {#sec-enforcement-phase-portraits}

In the distance--velocity $(d, v)$ phase plane, the stopping envelope separates states with enough clearance for the modeled stop from states without that reservation. Its boundary sets a speed ceiling under the stated braking and delay assumptions; crossing it does not prove that every possible maneuver ends in collision.

::: {#fig-12-stopping-envelope-phase-plane fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**Conditional stopping envelope**: For the warehouse mobile manipulator's base, a boundary separates states with modeled braking clearance from states that have already exhausted it. The inset includes the pre-brake delay, the matched stop suffix's jerk ramps, and the localization, protective, and tracking allowances. Clearance below the fixed allowances admits no approach speed, including zero. The curves use the accounted delay and stated braking envelope; unaccounted dispatch-to-admission time lowers the ceiling further." fig-alt="Phase portrait with obstacle distance on the horizontal axis and approach speed on the vertical axis. A braking-only parabola and an inset stopping boundary show the cost of pre-brake delay, the matched stop suffix, and the fixed allowances; a marker at the rack-end clear distance shows the speed ceiling, with the chosen aisle speed just below it."}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ CONDITIONAL STOPPING ENVELOPE (FIGURE)
# │ Context: @fig-12-stopping-envelope-phase-plane
# │ Goal:    show the speed ceiling clearance imposes, independent of throughput
# │ Show:    the viable set in the distance-velocity plane, and what pre-brake
# │          delay, the C2 stop, and the overheads cost relative to pure braking
# │ How:     tau v + d_S(v) + overhead <= d (@eq-enforce-stopping-envelope with
# │          the S-curve stop), solved by calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity
# │          at each clearance, from RM/AISLE
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import numpy as np
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.physics.robotics import calc_c2_stop_suffix, calc_max_permitted_velocity, calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity
from mlsysim.fmt import check
from mlsysim import viz

RM = Embodied.MobileManipulator.WarehouseMobileManipulator
AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle

# ┌── 1. LOAD ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A_BRAKE = AISLE.a_brake.to(meter / second**2).magnitude  # category: illustrative
TAU_DELAY = AISLE.tau_delay.to(second).magnitude  # category: derived
OVERHEAD = AISLE.fixed_overhead.to(meter).magnitude  # category: illustrative + chosen
D_CLEAR = AISLE.d_clear.to(meter).magnitude  # category: illustrative
V_AISLE = AISLE.v_aisle.to(meter / second).magnitude  # category: chosen
_v_ref = RM.base.max_velocity  # category: illustrative (drive limit)
J_BRAKE = calc_c2_stop_suffix(_v_ref, AISLE.a_brake)["peak_jerk"]  # category: derived (reference polynomial's peak jerk)

# ┌── 2. EXECUTE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def _ceiling_at(d):
    return (
        calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity(
            d * meter,
            AISLE.tau_delay,
            AISLE.a_brake,
            J_BRAKE,
            loc_margin=AISLE.delta_loc,
            physical_margin=AISLE.delta_margin + AISLE.eps_track,
        )
        .to(meter / second)
        .magnitude
    )

def v_admissible(d):
    """Largest v with tau v + d_S(v) + overhead <= d; NaN inside the fixed allowances."""
    d_arr = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(d, dtype=float))
    root = np.array([_ceiling_at(x) if x >= OVERHEAD else np.nan for x in d_arr])
    return root if np.ndim(d) else root[0]

v_braking_only = lambda d: np.sqrt(2.0 * A_BRAKE * d)  # constant deceleration, no delay or allowances
v_ceiling = float(v_admissible(D_CLEAR))

# ┌── 3. GUARD ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
check(abs(OVERHEAD - 0.190) < 1e-9, "Fixed overheads are 190 mm.")
# Closed form above a^2/j: constant braking at a_brake after tau + a/(2j)
_ceiling_ref = (
    calc_max_permitted_velocity(
        AISLE.d_clear,
        AISLE.tau_delay + AISLE.a_brake / (2 * J_BRAKE),
        AISLE.a_brake,
        loc_margin=AISLE.delta_loc,
        physical_margin=AISLE.delta_margin + AISLE.eps_track,
    )
    .to(meter / second)
    .magnitude
)
check(abs(v_ceiling - _ceiling_ref) < 1e-9, "The figure's ceiling must match the closed form above a^2/j.")
check(V_AISLE < v_ceiling, "The aisle speed sits inside the viable set.")
check(np.isnan(v_admissible(OVERHEAD / 2)), "No speed is admissible below the fixed clearance allowance.")
check(abs(float(v_admissible(OVERHEAD))) < 1e-12, "At exactly the fixed allowance, only zero approach speed fits.")

d = np.unique(np.append(np.linspace(0, 3.0, 500), OVERHEAD))

# ┌── 4. PLOT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax, COLORS, plt = viz.setup_plot(figsize=(8, 4.4))
ax.axvspan(0, OVERHEAD, color=COLORS["RedFill"], alpha=0.55, zorder=1)
ax.fill_between(d, v_admissible(d), 3.6, color=COLORS["RedFill"], alpha=0.55, zorder=1)
ax.fill_between(d, 0, v_admissible(d), color=COLORS["GreenFill"], alpha=0.55, zorder=1)
ax.plot(d, v_braking_only(d), color=COLORS["primary"], lw=1.5, ls=(0, (6, 3)), label="braking limit alone", zorder=4)
ax.plot(d, v_admissible(d), color=COLORS["BlueLine"], lw=2.4, label="conditional boundary (delay, $C^2$ stop, allowances)", zorder=5)

ax.text(0.55, 2.75, "forbidden set", color=COLORS["RedLine"], fontsize=9.5, fontweight="bold", ha="center", zorder=6)
ax.text(2.5, 0.22, "modeled viable set", color=COLORS["GreenLine"], fontsize=9.5, fontweight="bold", ha="center", zorder=6)

ax.plot([D_CLEAR], [v_ceiling], "o", ms=7, color=COLORS["BlueLine"], zorder=7)
ax.plot([D_CLEAR], [V_AISLE], "s", ms=5.5, color=COLORS["GreenLine"], zorder=7)
ax.vlines(D_CLEAR, 0, v_ceiling, color=COLORS["BlueLine"], lw=1.0, ls=(0, (1, 2)), zorder=4)
ax.hlines(v_ceiling, 0, D_CLEAR, color=COLORS["BlueLine"], lw=1.0, ls=(0, (1, 2)), zorder=4)
ax.annotate(
    f"rack end at {D_CLEAR:.2f} m\ncaps speed at {v_ceiling:.2f} m/s",
    xy=(D_CLEAR, v_ceiling),
    xytext=(D_CLEAR + 0.40, v_ceiling - 0.30),
    fontsize=9,
    color=COLORS["BlueLine"],
    ha="left",
    zorder=7,
    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color=COLORS["BlueLine"], lw=0.9),
)
ax.annotate(
    f"aisle speed {V_AISLE:.1f} m/s",
    xy=(D_CLEAR, V_AISLE),
    xytext=(D_CLEAR + 0.40, V_AISLE - 0.75),
    fontsize=9,
    color=COLORS["GreenLine"],
    ha="left",
    zorder=7,
    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color=COLORS["GreenLine"], lw=0.9),
)

ax.set_xlim(0, 3.0)
ax.set_ylim(0, 3.6)
ax.set_xlabel("Clearance to obstacle, $d$ (m)")
ax.set_ylabel("Velocity, $v$ (m/s)")
ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

:::
